questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Let $f(x)$ be differentiable on the interval $(0, \infty)$ such that $f(1)=1$ and
$\lim _{t \rightarrow x} \frac{t^2 f(x)-x^2 f(t)}{t-x}=1$ for each $x>0$
Then, $f(x)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, $\lim _{t \rightarrow x} \frac{t^2 f(x)-x^2 f(t)}{t-x}=1$
Using L' Hospital's rule, we get
$\lim _{t \rightarrow x} \frac{t^2 f^{\prime}(x)-2 x f(t)}{-1}=1\Rightarrow \quad x^2 f^{\prime}(x)-2 x f(x)+1=0\Rightarrow \quad \frac{x^2 f^{\prime}(x)-2 x f(x)}{\left(x^2\right)^2}+\frac{1}{x^4}=0\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d}{d x}\left(\frac{f(x)}{x^2}\right)=-\frac{1}{x^4}$
On integrating both sides, we get
$\frac{f(x)}{x^2}=+\frac{1}{3 x^3}+c \Rightarrow f(x)=\frac{1}{3 x}+c x^2$
Also, $\quad f(1)=1 \Rightarrow 1=\frac{1}{3 \times 1}+c(1)^2\Rightarrow \quad 1=\frac{1}{3}+c \Rightarrow \frac{2}{3}=c\therefore \quad f(x)=\frac{1}{3 x}+\frac{2 x^2}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $f(x)=\left[\frac{\sin x}{x}\right]+\left[\frac{2 \sin x}{x}\right]+\ldots+\left[\frac{10 \sin x}{x}\right]$ (where [.] is the largest integer). then, find the value of $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} f(x)$.
questions.solution:
As we know,
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin x}{x} \simeq 1$
but it is actually less than 1 .
So, $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left[\frac{\sin x}{x}\right]=0=1^2-1$
Similarly, $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left[2 \frac{\sin 2 x}{x}\right]=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left[4 \frac{\sin 2 x}{2 x}\right] =3=2^2-1$
Hence, $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left[n \frac{\sin n x}{x}\right]=n^2-1$
Therefore,
$\begin{aligned}
& \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} f(x)=\left(1^2-1\right)+\left(2^2-1\right)+\ldots+\left(10^2-(1)\right. \\
& =\left(1^2+2^2+\ldots+10^2\right)-(1+1+\ldots+1 \text{ times }) \\
& =\frac{10 \times 11 \times 21}{6}-10 \\
& =385-10=375
\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Given, $U_n=2+2^3+2^5+2^7+\ldots+2^{2 n+1}$
and $V_n=1+4+4^2+\ldots+4^{n-1}\therefore \quad U_n=\frac{l r-a}{r-1}=\frac{2^{2 n+1} \cdot 4-2}{4-1}=\frac{2^{2 n} \cdot 8-2}{3}$
and $\quad ' V_n=\frac{l r-a}{r-1}=\frac{4^{n-1} \cdot 4-1}{4-1}=\frac{2^{2 n}-1}{3}$

questions.q: The value of $\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left\{\frac{a_1^{1 / x}+a_2^{1 / x}+\ldots+a_n^{1 / x}}{n}\right\}^{n x}$, is
questions.solution:
Let $x=\frac{1}{y}$. Then,
$\begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left\{\frac{a_1^{1 / x}+a_2^{1 / x}+\ldots+a_n^{1 / x}}{n}\right\}^{n x} \\ &=\lim _{y \rightarrow 0}\left\{\frac{a_1^y+a_2^y+\ldots+a_n^y}{n}\right\}^{n / y} \\ &=\lim _{y \rightarrow 0}\left\{1+\frac{a_1^y+a_2^y+\ldots+a_n^y-n}{n}\right\}^{n / y} \\ &=e^{y \rightarrow 0}\left[\frac{a_1^y-1}{y}+\frac{a_2^y-1}{y}+\ldots+\frac{a_n^y-1}{y}\right\} \\ &=e^{\log a_1+\log a_2+\ldots+\log a_n} \\ &=e^{\log \left(a_1 a_2 \ldots a_n\right)} \\ &=a_1 a_2 a_3 \ldots a_n\end{aligned}$

$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\sin \sin 0-\sin 0}{a(0)^3+b(0)^5+c}=-\frac{1}{12}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{0}{c}=-\frac{1}{12} \Rightarrow c=0$
Applying L' Hospital's rule in Eq.(i),we get
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\cos (\sin x) \cos x-\cos x}{3 a x^2+5 b x^4+0}=-\frac{1}{12}\Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\cos x(\cos (\sin x)-1)}{x^2(3 a+5 b x)}=-\frac{1}{12}\Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \cos x \frac{2 \sin ^2\left(\frac{\sin x}{2}\right)}{x^2(3 a+5 b x)}=-\frac{1}{12}\Rightarrow \frac{\cos 0}{3 a+5 b \times 0} \times \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{2 \sin ^2\left(\frac{\sin x}{2}\right)}{4\left(\frac{\sin x}{2}\right)^2 \times\left(\frac{x}{\sin x}\right)^2}=-\frac{1}{12}\Rightarrow \frac{1}{3 a+0} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{1}=-\frac{1}{12}\left(\because \lim _{\theta \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin \theta}{\theta}=1\right)\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{6 a}=-\frac{1}{12} \Rightarrow 6 a=-12\therefore \quad a=-2$
Hence, $a=-2, b \in \mathbb{R}$ and $c=0$

questions.solution: $\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{\left[\sum_{K=1}^{100} x^K\right]-100}{(x-1)}\begin{aligned} & =\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{\left(x+x^2+x^3+\ldots+x^{100}\right)-100}{(x-1)} \\ & =\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{(x-1)+\left(x^2-1\right)+\left(x^3-1\right)+\ldots+\left(x^{100}-1\right)}{(x-1)}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1}\left\{\left(\frac{x-1}{x-1}\right)+\left(\frac{x^2-1}{x-1}\right)+\left(\frac{x^3-1}{x-1}\right)\right. & \\ & \left.+\ldots+\left(\frac{x^{100}-1}{x-1}\right)\right\}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1}\left(\frac{x-1}{x-1}\right)+\lim _{x \rightarrow 1}\left(\frac{x^2-1}{x-1}\right) & +\lim _{x \rightarrow 1}\left(\frac{x^3-1}{x-1}\right) \\ & +\ldots+\lim _{x \rightarrow 1}\left(\frac{x^{100}-1}{x-1}\right)\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =1+2+3+\ldots+100 \\ & =\Sigma 100=\frac{100 \times(100+1)}{2}\end{aligned}=50 \times 101=5050 \quad\left\{\because \Sigma n=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right\}$.

questions.solution: Let $y=\frac{x}{x+\frac{\sqrt[3]{x}}{x+\sqrt[3]{x} \ldots \text{ infinity }}}=\frac{x}{x+\frac{1}{x^{2 / 3}} \cdot \frac{x}{x+\sqrt[3]{x} \ldots \infty}}=\frac{x}{x+\frac{y}{x^{2 / 3}}}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow y=\frac{x^{5 / 3}}{x^{5 / 3}+y} \\ & \Rightarrow y^2+\left(x^{5 / 3}\right) \cdot y-x^{5 / 3}=0 \\ & \therefore \quad y=\frac{-x^{5 / 3} \pm \sqrt{x^{10 / 3}+4 x^{5 / 3}}}{2}\end{aligned}=\frac{-x^{5 / 3}+\sqrt{x^{10 / 3}+4 x^{5 / 3}}}{2}(\because y>0)\begin{aligned} & =\frac{4 x^{5 / 3}}{2\left(\sqrt{x^{10 / 3}+4 x^{5 / 3}}+x^{5 / 3}\right)}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{\left(1+\frac{4}{x^{5 / 3}}\right)+1}} \\ & \begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} y=\frac{2}{\sqrt{1+0}+1} \\ & \quad=\frac{2}{2}=1.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
If $f(x)= \begin{cases}\frac{\sin [x]}{[x]}, & {[x] \neq 0} \\ 0, & {[x]=0}\end{cases}$
where $[x]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$, then $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} f(x)$ equals
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{ As, } f(x)= \begin{cases}\frac{\sin [x]}{[x]}, & {[x] \neq 0} \\
0, & {[x]=0}\end{cases} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad f(x)= \begin{cases}\frac{\sin [x]}{[x]}, & x \in R-[0,1) \\
0, & 0 \leq x < 1\end{cases} \\
& \therefore \quad \text{ RHL at } x=0 \\
& \lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin [0+h]}{[0+h]}=0 \\
& \text{ LHL at } x=0 \\
& \lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} f(x)=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin [0-h]}{[0-h]} \\
& =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin (-1)}{-1}=\sin 1
\end{aligned}$
Since, RHL ≠ LHL
$\therefore$ Limit does not exist.

questions.q: The value of $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\int_0^{x^2} \cos ^2 t d t}{x \sin x}$ is
questions.solution:
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\int_0^{x^2} \cos ^2 t d t}{x \sin x}$
Using L Hospital's rule, we get $\begin{aligned} & =\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\cos ^2\left(x^2\right) \cdot 2 x-0}{x \cos x+\sin x} \\ & =\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{2 \cos ^2\left(x^2\right)}{\cos x+\frac{\sin x}{x}} \\ & =\frac{2}{2}=1 \end{aligned}$

Let $f(x)=\frac{|\sin x|}{x}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $f: R \rightarrow R$ be such that $f(1)=3$ and $f^{\prime}(1)=6$. Then, $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left[\frac{f(1+x)}{f(1)}\right]^{1 / x}$ equals
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{ Let } \quad y=\left[\frac{f(1+x)}{f(1)}\right]^{1 / x} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \log y=\frac{1}{x}[\log f(1+x)-\log f(1)] \\
& \Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \log y=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{[\log f(1+x)-\log f(1)]}{x} \\
& \Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \log y=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left[\frac{1}{f(1+x)} f^{\prime}(1+x)\right] \\
& \text{ (using L' Hospital's rule) } \\
& =\frac{f^{\prime}(1)}{f(1)}=\frac{6}{3}=2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} y=e^2
\end{aligned}$
